subject: C21
required_fixes: C21-R2-F1 (high; original F1 partly open): Propagate turn cancellation to the admitted runtime operations, including queued work. authority/harness_tools.rs:376 cancels only the run future; after admit_management (:424) its OperationId is discarded while ManagementHandle::result merely waits. The scan branch likewise admits an independent operation without linking its lifetime to the turn. Dropping these waits does not call Operations::cancel: runtime.rs later claims queued work using its own cancellation token. With the four active slots occupied, a tool read/scan admitted to the queue can therefore dispatch after Stop/End while the tenant context remains current. The new slow-read test waits until management_reads > 0, so it proves late-result suppression for already-dispatched work, not cancellation before dispatch. Acceptance: hold runtime capacity, queue actual management and scan tools, interrupt/end the turn, then release capacity; queued operations must settle NotSent and make no remote request. Cover cancellation/timeout cleanup and retain honest outcomes for work already dispatched. Keep the new run/turn lease protection for stale results.

C21-R2-F2 (high; original F2 partly open): Fail closed when JSON-bearing result strings cannot be inspected within the decoding bounds. harness/tools.rs:415 opens JSON strings only while depth < 4 and size <= 4 MiB, then leaves deeper strings untouched; scrub ignores strings. A small management-page item containing five nested JSON-string metadata wrappers around an Authorization field therefore still sends its credential canary to the model. The supplied canary cases exercise shallower encodings only. Preserve the bounded decoder, but omit/reject or safely replace still-encoded data at its inspection limit rather than forwarding it unfiltered. Acceptance: production management page/detail tool fixtures with more than four encoded layers and boundary-sized JSON strings expose no credential canary; ordinary safe metadata remains available.

C21-R2-F3 (medium; original F3 partly open): Establish complete file-change scope before allowing approval. harness/session.rs:1547 filters out changes without paths, takes only 64 paths and cuts each path to 1024 bytes; :1365 then treats any nonempty cached list as reviewable. Thus an approval may authorize additional files beyond the displayed list or an effect-bearing path suffix hidden by truncation. The command-length fix is sound, but the same fail-closed rule is not applied to file metadata. Acceptance: preserve and show every complete bounded path, or decline the request when the original change list cannot be represented completely. Test more than 64 changes, a path beyond the display bound and an incomplete change entry; none may be approved from a partial list. The pinned patch helper's currently disclosed write failure does not establish complete approval scope.

C21-R2-F4 (medium; new truncation regression): Enforce MAX_RESULT_BYTES on the final serialized envelope. harness/tools.rs:398 truncates the already-serialized result to MAX_RESULT_BYTES - 512, then JSON-escapes that prefix again inside partial without checking the resulting length. Quotes/backslashes expand: the inspected algorithm applied to an ASCII safe field containing 20,000 quote characters yields a 48,203-byte envelope against the declared 24,576-byte limit. It can also exceed the engine budget the code reserves space for. Acceptance: every final result remains valid JSON and <= MAX_RESULT_BYTES for quote-, backslash-, control-character- and multibyte-heavy inputs, with a truthful cut note and preserved secret filtering.
evidence_gaps: C21-R2-G1: Native C21-N04 still does not establish that all affected filenames were shown before Allow. acceptance_c21.py:90 captures only text starting with Run a command, Change files or In /; :242 sets file_change_shown from the Change files title, and evaluate accepts that title as the whole-scope check. The retained successful approval observation contains four Change files strings and no filename; tree-write.json is captured after the turn. This is an evidence limitation, not proof that the normal added.txt row was absent. Capture/assert the actual pending Files region and exact complete paths before approval, or retain the observed automatic decline when metadata is unavailable. The checker must fail if a displayed file is omitted or truncated.
limitations: Independent read-only review: no application fixes, mutating test/build reruns, application/engine launches, product endpoint calls or credential access. Cancellation, encoded-secret and partial-file findings follow inspected production control flow; they are not claimed as newly executed Rust integration reproductions.

All four supplied fingerprints match independently recomputed values. Verified the 689-entry source inventory, 375 referenced hashes, run logs/artifacts, shared input/scratch/installed equivalence and C20 attempt-03's authentic passing 9/10 predecessor receipt. No transport or frozen-input blocker was found.

The new run/turn leases correctly prevent a stale ToolResult from satisfying a reused request ID, and interruption rejects new calls at the session boundary. However, dropping the sink future does not cancel an operation already admitted into the runtime queue. The recorded test covers a slow request after dispatch; R2-F1 specifies the missing queue boundary.

Original F4's replacement bound is addressed by upsert. An independent in-memory probe of the production TypeScript validator accepted the earlier 1,047,548-byte started snapshot, rejected the unbounded 1,055,750-byte completion, and accepted the 1,045,500-byte snapshot after modeling the inspected Rust eviction rule. Rust upsert itself was inspected through its unit test and mutation evidence, not independently executed. The result-envelope size example is independent ASCII JSON byte arithmetic, not a claim of a Rust runtime rerun.

The new offline/reconnect integration and native N09 cover pending approval/proposal invalidation, local protected history/project state and no automatic resume or resubmission after relaunch. They improve the prior T23 gap. The queued-operation boundary and native complete-file evidence remain as specified above.

Recorded checks pass 408 frontend tests and 211 core unit tests. Scoped runs pass nine harness_tools tests, 21 identity/history tests, twelve IPC tests and 153 selected frontend tests; selected counts overlap the full suite. All 35 submitted mutations detect their named guards, with five baseline targets passing three runs each. These results do not exercise the remaining boundary cases.

Nine recorded C21 native checks pass on fixture executable 26558e5c421d055035d7d1534fbb253dff78602ebc46d14fe70fdf4dcf681072. The driver/observations support project selection, command approval/denial, sandbox negatives, operator-owned proposal review/Apply, keyboard navigation and offline reconnect, subject to R2-G1. The patch helper still fails inside the pinned sandbox as disclosed; approved shell writes are the demonstrated write path.

Recomputed workload statistics fit the registered limits: tool read p95 217.20 ms, approval 167.69 ms, approved command 170.36 ms, proposal staging 137.08 ms, review-ready 13.89 ms and peak process-tree RSS 461.2 MiB. These are recorded synthetic-fixture measurements. Live model/management/Gateway qualification remains C25, signed installed-package qualification C26, and spoken VoiceOver is not recorded.

Architecture remains 9 for the focused typed-tool module, existing native domain admission, proposal/review separation and native project binding. Behavior, authority/security and validation remain 8 because the specific cancellation, filtering, approval and result-bound defects prevent the full gate. This verdict covers C21; it does not approve C22 or cumulative P06.
